Compare facts, missing information, examination candidates, contraindication flags, human review escalation and evidence ID traceability against expert-labeled gold JSON. # Medical AI Laboratory — Clinical Tool Development

**Mission:** develop modular, disease-specific **clinical decision-support and diagnostic workflow tools** for eventual use by qualified healthcare professionals. The project is currently in the **research and prototype-development stage**: no component has established clinical safety, effectiveness, regulatory clearance, or authorization for routine patient care. The target product is a collection of usable clinical tools, not merely a benchmarking repository or a standalone large language model.

**Intended future workflow:** clinical intake → indication and examination selection → data acquisition and QC → specialist model-assisted findings and measurements → evidence-linked draft report → clinician-reviewed diagnostic interpretation and management options → documented follow-up. Every clinical decision remains under accountable professional oversight until and unless a separately validated and appropriately authorized tool is established.

**Research areas:** clinical AI tools, medical imaging AI, open-source medical models, diagnostic decision support, ultrasound, chest X-ray, CT, MRI, medical image segmentation, MedGemma benchmarks, dataset evaluation, and agent-assisted clinical software development.

[Discoverability and research topic index](docs/DISCOVERABILITY.md) · [Medical AI model analysis](research/imaging/model-integration-registry.md) · [Clinical disease workflows](diseases/README.md) · [Evaluation and benchmark research](evaluation/README.md)

## Development status: planning first, implementation later

**The clinical tools have not been developed yet.** This repository is presently a **research, requirements, architecture and agent-planning workspace**. Existing Python scripts, JSON schemas, benchmark examples and installation helpers are exploratory infrastructure/prototypes; they are **not** implemented clinical products or evidence that disease workflows function end to end.

**Future implementation will be generated iteratively using OpenCode agents**, with human review and explicit project decisions before each increment. Agent configurations and skills currently describe intended work; they do not mean that agents have executed the work, created the external model forks, downloaded datasets, trained models, tested hardware, or validated clinical functions.

### Planned agent-led development sequence

1. **Requirements and intended-use definition:** select one clinical tool/disease and define users, patient setting, supported actions, exclusions, safety boundaries and acceptance criteria.
2. **Architecture and agent plan:** design the model selection/forking agent, source/weight/license audit agent, dataset agent, adapter/implementation agent, model evaluation agent, integration agent, UI agent and quality/safety reviewer. Specify responsibilities, input/output contracts, human approval gates and execution order.
3. **Research and model selection:** inventory all applicable small/pretrained models, legal terms and exact releases; decide whether each source requires a fork or a pinned dependency.
4. **Dataset and test design:** find legally usable datasets, expert reference labels, versioning, partitioning, metrics and pass/fail criteria **before** implementing or running model tests.
5. **Incremental code generation:** direct OpenCode to implement one bounded, testable component at a time; review every generated change, dependency and model checkpoint.
6. **Independent component evaluation:** test each candidate model on appropriate task-specific data and hardware; record actual performance, failures, abstentions and provenance.
7. **Clinical workflow integration:** assemble qualified components into one disease-specific tool; test interfaces, audit trail, interoperability and error propagation.
8. **Later clinical and regulatory work:** plan evidence generation and approvals separately; no direct patient-care deployment without the required validation and authorization.

**Not yet completed:** clinical tool implementation, operational agent orchestration, external model forks, all-model benchmarks, full 50-disease runtime pipelines, clinician validation, and clinical deployment. These are **planned deliverables**, not completed features.

## Workflow

1. Select a disease or checkup from `diseases/registry.csv`.
2. Create or refine `diseases/<slug>/procedure.json`, with patient entrypoint, required/optional tests and dependencies. Tests **need not involve imaging**.
3. Identify source-linked clinical guidelines, suitable datasets and model registries; mark unavailable, restricted, or unsupported cases explicitly.
4. Evaluate each JSON step **separately**: context, red flags, examination selection, quality control, findings, diagnostic synthesis, reporting, management evidence and follow-up.
5. Retain per-step prediction provenance, evaluation dataset version, model weights/commit, reference labels, metrics, error analysis, human review, and auditable results.
6. Only afterward study end-to-end propagation of errors. A single strong AI benchmark does not establish clinical safety.

## Multi-model analysis and new-model development

The project evaluates **multiple specialized models**, not just MedGemma. Each disease may combine clinical text extraction, examination selection, quality control, segmentation, detection, interpretation and clinician-reviewed guideline evidence. Different models can also compete for the **same task**. A model is never assumed valid for a disease simply because its upstream repository is available.

### Available analysis options

| Analysis track | Representative existing models/tools | Evaluation questions |
|---|---|---|
| Clinical context and reporting | MedGemma 1.5, medSpaCy, CheXbert, RadGraph, Whisper (transcription) | Facts, missing context, contradictions, hallucinations, missed red flags, source fidelity |
| Ultrasound | EchoNet-Dynamic, SonoNet, MedSAM (prompted segmentation) | Correct plane, left-ventricular measurement error, anatomy masks, patient/site shift |
| Chest X-ray | TorchXRayVision, CheXzero, MedGemma | Per-finding sensitivity/specificity, label uncertainty, out-of-domain errors |
| CT | TotalSegmentator, task-specific MONAI bundles, LUNA16 benchmark implementations | Segmentation Dice and measurement error, nodule sensitivity/false positives per scan |
| MRI | MRIQC, ANTsPyNet, task-specific MONAI models, MedSAM | QC sensitivity, region masks, lesion reference labels, sequence/site robustness |
| Microscopy/pathology | HoVer-Net, Cellpose, QuPath, HistoQC | Nucleus masks, tissue artifacts, classification error and scanner/stain shift |
| Physiological signals | WFDB, NeuroKit2, task-specific ECG classifiers to verify | Signal quality, patient-level sensitivity, rhythm classification; not image interpretation |
| Clinical information systems | HAPI FHIR, OHIF, Orthanc, Medplum | Data provenance, interface correctness, report delivery, acknowledgement and follow-up |

These are **research candidates and infrastructure**, not an approved set of clinical diagnostic models. Some have pretrained checkpoints and some are frameworks, benchmarks or non-AI tools; weight access, code/data licenses and independent validation must be reviewed for each.

### Model selection and development decision

1. **Define the target and reference standard**: disease, patient group, imaging or non-imaging examination, intended outcome, and human review.
2. **Inventory alternatives**: use the [model integration registry](research/imaging/model-integration-registry.md) and [fork manifest](automation/model-forks.json). Distinguish a reusable pretrained model from a framework needing task-specific weights.
3. **Use the same authorized cases where comparable**: lock dataset and split using [DVC governance](evaluation/README.md), verify train/test contamination and licensing, freeze prompts and preprocessing.
4. **Test each model separately**: record exact version, weights, input/output JSON contract, reference labels, task metrics, confidence intervals where feasible, latency, peak GPU/CPU RAM, abstentions and failures.
5. **Compare only like-for-like outputs**: classification against classification, segmentation against segmentation, measurement against reference measurement, and clinical context against adjudicated context. A Dice score cannot be compared directly with medical-text F1.
6. **Test multi-model integration**: evaluate errors propagated between image quality, anatomy, finding detection and report generation; verify that a failed early stage cannot turn into a confident downstream diagnosis or management suggestion.
7. **Develop a new model only for a verified gap**: start with a deterministic baseline or pretrained model; consider calibration or parameter-efficient adaptation if permitted; train from scratch only when evidence, labeled data, rights and computing resources justify it. The developer's **8 GB RTX 4060** is one reproducible benchmark target, **not** the deployment minimum, maximum, or constraint for everyone. Profile model training and inference separately for CPU-only, low-memory, mid-range and high-memory systems.
8. **Release only research outputs with traceability**: write per-step scores/results into [disease procedure JSON](pipeline/README.md) and a model evaluation card. Human specialist verification remains mandatory before any clinical care decision; no autonomous treatment or prescription.

### Example composition: lightweight, task-specific components

**Default architecture: no large language model required.** Start with small, task-specific pretrained models, deterministic rules, or manual specialist review. MedGemma is an **optional benchmark comparator**, not a mandatory stage. Actual GPU memory, system RAM and CPU-only feasibility must be measured across hardware tiers, never assumed from the developer's machine.

```text
Patient intake        → structured form + medSpaCy (rule-based extraction)
Examination selection → guideline lookup + deterministic eligibility rules + clinician
Image QC              → metadata/geometry checks; SonoNet for fetal planes only
Anatomy/measurement   → small task-specific segmentation model or manual measurement
Finding detection     → a verified small specialist classifier; otherwise MODEL_GAP
Reporting             → structured templates with linked source observations
Management evidence   → versioned guideline retrieval and clinician review
Follow-up             → deterministic task tracking and result acknowledgement
```

For a concrete **cardiac ultrasound** research task, [EchoNet-Dynamic](https://github.com/echonet/dynamic) is a candidate for ejection-fraction assessment; for chest radiographs, a selected [TorchXRayVision](https://github.com/mlmed/torchxrayvision) checkpoint is an alternative. Both require actual checkpoint, licensing, accuracy and memory audits before use. **Do not combine unrelated modality models into one disease pipeline.** Use classical image analysis or a smaller approved model when a deep network is unnecessary.

Evaluate any candidate against a non-AI baseline and optionally against [MedGemma](evaluation/medgemma-technical-clinical-analysis.md) *only on compatible tasks with identical independent reference cases*. The disease JSON must identify exactly which components were evaluated and where clinician approval is required.

## Product development stages and clinical readiness gates

| Stage | Deliverable | Exit requirement |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Research and planning (current)** | Disease needs analysis, model inventory/forks, evidence and benchmark datasets, exploratory clinical workflow designs | Document precise intended use, target users/patients, risks, reference standards and repeatable evaluation |
| **2. Engineering prototype** | Runnable end-to-end software with verified model adapters, interfaces, traceable outputs, privacy protections and secure data processing | Integration tests, role separation, logging, error handling, versioned build, reproducible performance |
| **3. Clinical evaluation** | Locked intended-use system evaluated on representative independent clinical cases with appropriate clinician oversight | Predefined safety/performance endpoints, expert adjudication, bias and site-shift analysis, prospective study if appropriate |
| **4. Regulatory and quality review** | Jurisdiction-specific classification, risk management, quality system, clinical evidence, security and monitoring documentation | Applicable regulatory and institutional approvals; clearance/certification when legally required |
| **5. Controlled clinical deployment** | Clinician-facing installation, instructions, monitoring, rollback and post-deployment change control | Authorized use only, with human accountability and ongoing safety/performance monitoring |

A benchmark success or a GitHub fork is **not** evidence of clinical readiness. Each tool must specify its **intended clinical purpose**, end user, care environment, eligible patients, contraindicated/missing inputs, expected clinician action, claims supported by evidence and escalation/human-review behavior. ### 3. Reproducible procedure for evaluating one model

```bash
# Read model-specific procedures and approved dataset status
python3 scripts/check_datasets.py
python3 scripts/check_disease_dataset_catalog.py

# Verify source-code metrics and synthetic pipeline (NO real model scored)
python3 scripts/run_evaluation_pipeline.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' -v

# Preview dataset acquisition. Download only after rights + HTTPS + checksum audit
python3 scripts/download_dataset.py --dataset DATASET_ID

# Evaluate a real model only after compatible model adapter and datasets exist
# /evaluate-model DISEASE_SLUG MODEL_ID    (inside OpenCode)
```

**Individual tests:** use dedicated task metrics. Classification: sensitivity/specificity, precision/NPV, calibration; segmentation: Dice/IoU and boundary distances; detection: FROC and false positives per scan; quantitative measurement: MAE, bias; context: fact extraction, omissions and escalations. Document confidence intervals, test prevalence, baseline and failures. The committed Python implementation currently provides **binary and structured-context scorers**, not every specialty metric.

### 4. Multi-model comparison — after individual qualification

- For each disease JSON stage, identify **every relevant candidate** from the registry (e.g., more than one CXR classifier), the deterministic/non-AI baseline and an optional general model such as MedGemma.
- Use exactly the same *authorized, task-matched* held-out cases and reference standard for like-for-like comparisons; otherwise mark `NOT_COMPARABLE`. Pin prompts, thresholds, weights and preprocessing.
- Compare model performance, abstention, false-negative risks, resource cost, model size and failure modes. Never combine scores for incompatible tasks (e.g., segmentation Dice with textual F1).
- Test ensembles/routing only after measuring their **incremental gain and error propagation**, including whether a weak QC model degrades an otherwise strong detection model.
- Record a separate JSON result for each model × disease × procedure step. A successful component test **does not certify the full workflow**.
- MedGemma remains an **optional research comparator**, not the baseline requirement or a compulsory component.

[JSON procedure contract](pipeline/README.md) · [Model-by-model integration list](research/imaging/model-integration-registry.md) · [MedGemma comparison](evaluation/medgemma-50-disease-pipeline.md)

### 5. End-to-end test — each of the 50 disease pathways

For a representative, expert-reviewed case, validate: **patient intake → red-flag/missing-context review → screening/diagnostic examination decision (including no imaging) → appropriate acquisition/QC → anatomical localization → disease finding model(s) → uncertainty and specialist report → clinician-controlled guideline evidence → results acknowledgement and follow-up**.

For every step, record `entrypoint`, `depends_on`, `required`, `input_keys`, `output_keys`, model ID/revision, independent dataset, `evaluation.status`, artifact path, abstention policy and human-review requirement in `diseases/<slug>/procedure.json`. The [interpreter](scripts/interpret_procedure.py) currently **plans and validates** steps, but **does not run** arbitrary medical models. Full care-path tests need separate compatible adapters, reviewed data and source-verified guidelines; no automatic treatment selection or prescribing.

### 6. Completion gates and progress ledger

The **minimum project completion bar** is: (a) all 41 upstream entries receive a documented fork/dependency disposition and license audit; (b) each usable model has a runnable smoke test and reproducible *individual* evaluation or explicit reason it cannot be tested; (c) all applicable models for each of the 50 diseases are compared on valid cases; (d) each disease has a reviewed stage-by-stage JSON procedure and end-to-end error-handling test; and (e) everything is referenced by Git/DVC revisions and evaluation reports. **None of these milestones is automatically complete merely because its Markdown description exists.**

**Actual status:** inventory and planning code committed; actual forks, full-dataset downloads, all-model inference, external clinical validation, and 50-disease integrated tests are **not completed**. Published upstream paper scores must never be labeled as local measurements.

- **Documented:** 50 starting clinical conditions and disease folders; candidate open-source projects/datasets; modality research; JSON procedure and evaluation specifications.

**Evidence standards:** cite actual academic studies and clinical guidelines; separate the paper's result from our locally measured output; expose uncertainty, incomplete coverage and limitations.

### Model-specific acceptance workflow

For **each manifest entry** the work sequence is:
1. Open `https://github.com/OWNER/REPO`; verify exact origin, branch, active maintenance, license and security status.
2. Read the linked *peer-reviewed paper* when available, making a note if the paper evidence is pending.
3. Find exact pretrained model checkpoint (if this is a trained model) and document checksum, data/license, input/output schema.
4. Measure whether inference works on the available CPU/RAM (and optional GPU) with no training; distinguish unavailable weights from unsupported modality.
5. Decide: fork to maintain patches; install pinned dependency for unmodified code; or defer.
6. If forking, use the agent and record fork metadata; optionally create submodule in `external/models/`.
7. Add a **separate** wrapper/adapter and test in the product codebase. Commit `git add`, `git commit`, `git push` only after reviewing changes.
8. Document clinically relevant accuracy, domain shift, test set, external validation, failures and clinician review, or explicitly mark **not yet verified**.

**No forks or CPU benchmarks have been executed from ChatGPT.**

# Disease JSON workflow contract

**One disease = one declarative `procedure.json`.** It defines the starting event, ordered steps, per-step evaluation, model reference, input/output contracts and dependencies. The interpreter performs **static validation and safe simulation**, not medical inference or autonomous treatment.

Each step contains:
- `id`, `kind`, `depends_on`, `required`
- `input_keys`, `output_keys` for typed data handoffs
- `executor`: `human`, `rule`, `model`, or `none`
- `model`: explicit `registry_id` and `version` for model steps, or null
- `evaluation`: `dataset_id`, `metric`, `target`, `status`, `result_path` (per-step, never inherited from another model)
- `evidence_status`: `pending` or `verified`
- `approval_required`: true at clinical interpretation and management steps

A model step with missing evaluation, weights or adapter must **not run**. An evaluation status of `passed` is a recorded assertion requiring independent evidence; this interpreter does not trust it as clinical authorization. A model output is never interpreted as a final diagnosis. Checkup eligibility and imaging must be evaluated per disease and patient context.

# MedGemma 1.5 4B — local 8 GB RTX 4060 evaluation

[MedGemma comparison research](../../evaluation/medgemma-50-disease-pipeline.md) · [Model card](https://developers.google.com/health-ai-developer-foundations/medgemma/model-card) · [Official weights](https://huggingface.co/google/medgemma-1.5-4b-it)

## Suitability

Google's 4B model is the appropriate local candidate for an NVIDIA RTX 4060 with **8 GB VRAM**. Google's approximate 4-bit static weight footprint is **3.4 GB**, with runtime, activation/image encoder and KV-cache overhead additional. The 27B model is not a sensible fit for 8 GB. Local operation is free of per-request API charges, but **requires acceptance of Google's Health AI Developer Foundations terms**, internet download, disk space and compatible CUDA drivers. No commercial or clinical clearance implied.

**Use:** Start with text-only structured clinical context on *fabricated* cases. MedGemma supports images but CT/MRI 3D and whole slide pathology require special preprocessing and may not fit this 8GB configuration; do not assume all modality paths work.

## Step 1: Prepare WSL Python and GPU

```bash
cd ~/projects/medical-ai-labo-analysis
git pull origin main
nvidia-smi                    # confirm 8 GB NVIDIA GPU is exposed in WSL
python3 -m venv .venv-medgemma
source .venv-medgemma/bin/activate
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
# Install CUDA-enabled PyTorch for your NVIDIA driver/CUDA compatibility:

## Step 2: Accept model terms and sign in

Open [google/medgemma-1.5-4b-it](https://huggingface.co/google/medgemma-1.5-4b-it), accept the model agreement with your own account, and log in locally:

```

Downloads default to `models/weights/medgemma-1.5-4b-it/`, which is Git-ignored. Use `--revision COMMIT_SHA` to pin an exact model revision, and record this plus hashes for reproducible evaluation. ## Step 3: 4-bit test

```bash
python3 models/medgemma-local/infer.py
```

The script loads the official weights using Transformers + bitsandbytes 4-bit NF4 double quantization, one CUDA GPU, and small `max_new_tokens`. It tests a **synthetic text-only vignette**. It writes generated text, runtime and measured PyTorch peak allocated VRAM to `evaluation/results/medgemma-local-smoke.json` (Git-ignored). Peak allocation is not total `nvidia-smi` VRAM consumption. The script has **not** been executed on your RTX 4060, so actual memory fit and output validity are unknown. If out of memory: free other GPU processes, reduce prompt/image complexity, use fewer new tokens or an officially compatible prequantized runtime after verifying format/rights. Do not silently offload large fractions to limited system RAM.

## Step 4: Compare, don't assume

The smoke JSON is **not** a medical accuracy result. An adapter must first convert actual expert-labeled independent evaluation cases into the same structured schema as `scripts/evaluate_context.py`. Do not reuse training cases for test. Run an identical specialist or rule-based baseline, measure field-level F1, missed safety flags, guideline appropriateness, abstention, RAM, latency and generalization. Use `scripts/compare_context_models.py` only after both systems produce **case-matched structured predictions**.

- 8 GB **GPU VRAM** does not equal 8 GB total system RAM; WSL may also have strict RAM caps.
- No patient data should be entered into smoke prompts, committed to Git, or sent to outside services.
- For CT/MRI/ultrasound, verify image/volume preprocessing and independently validate each pathway.

## Staged integration concept
1. Start with **deidentified/synthetic encounter**, keep source text and patient provenance.
2. Extract clinician-verifiable information and link appropriate guideline evidence; **clinician approves** investigation.
3. Ingest real available examination, validate identifiers and quality with modality-specific checks.
4. Use appropriately licensed pretrained components for *defined anatomical structures*.
5. Run narrowly scoped, externally evaluated finding models where available; otherwise explicitly state **no model available / not evaluated**.
6. Present machine findings alongside actual image and raw evidence; draft only a clinician-reviewed report.
7. Show applicable, sourced guidance but do not prescribe individualized treatment autonomously.
8. Record acknowledgements, actions and follow-up; expose unresolved findings.

**Alternative flows:** no imaging necessary, failed examination quality, pathology/laboratory after imaging, multiple concurrent tests, further testing required, unavailable model, clinician disagreement, emergency escalation, inability to reach patient.

## Engineering contracts
Each module returns: `patient_pseudonym`, `encounter_id`, `study_id` when appropriate, `source_type`, `created_at`, `evidence_links`, `software_version`, `weights_version`, `input_quality`, `output`, `uncertainty`, `human_review_status`, `audit_event_id`. Missing outputs remain missing rather than being fabricated.

For true clinical settings, de-identification, consent/lawful basis, access logging, security, privacy, cybersecurity, regulatory classification and specialist evaluation precede deployment.

## Decision framework
For each component evaluate: (a) peer-reviewed task validation and external cohorts; (b) open source **and** pretrained weights availability; (c) data and commercial licensing; (d) compute resources/latency on CPU; (e) safe failure mode; (f) competing solutions; (g) measurable clinical workflow benefit. Clinical benefit is not established simply because a GitHub project exists.

## Review conclusions
- First prototype candidate: **study metadata + quality checks + source-linked imaging report workflow** using public/synthetic data and deterministic tools.
- Second: specialist pretrained segmentation (one anatomically defined task).
- Third: clinically meaningful finding detection and cross-modal synthesis only after dedicated external validation.
- The goal is a *human-supervised modular diagnostic research platform*, not a universal autonomous doctor.

## Correct comparator

Google's **MedGemma 1.5 4B** (January 2026) is an open-weight multimodal medical text/image model. It is **not** a specialized binary detector or guaranteed clinical decision maker. [Google launch](https://research.google/blog/next-generation-medical-image-interpretation-with-medgemma-15-and-medical-speech-to-text-with-medasr/) · [Official model card](https://huggingface.co/google/medgemma-1.5-4b-it). Its weights have Health AI Developer Foundations terms, not ordinary unrestricted OSS licensing. Verify current terms. MedASR is separate medical speech transcription software.

**Do not conflate:** Google's Med-Gemini/AMIE research systems, the general Gemini commercial API, and downloadable MedGemma weights. They differ in accessibility, modality and validated performance.

## What to compare

| Task | General model candidate | Specialized comparator | Metric |
|---|---|---|---|
| Clinical-context facts/missing items | MedGemma 1.5 4B text | Rule-based extractor or medSpaCy | Field-level precision/recall/F1, false safety omissions |
| Clinical test decision support | MedGemma with verified guideline excerpts | Clinician-authored retrieval/rules | Expert-agreement and guideline source precision, unsafe routing |
| Chest X-ray finding labels | MedGemma 1.5 image/text | TorchXRayVision / CheXzero | Per-label sensitivity, specificity, AUROC where probabilities available |
| Echo LV ejection fraction | MedGemma (only if verified modality support) | EchoNet-Dynamic | MAE, RMSE, bias and clinical interpretation error |
| CT anatomic localization | MedGemma 1.5 | TotalSegmentator | Dice/IoU, lesion- or region-specific findings |
| Medical reporting | MedGemma | Specialist source-linked templates | Hallucination rate, missed positives, negative/uncertain handling |

For modality-incompatible tasks, record **NOT_COMPARABLE** rather than forcing a score. MedGemma may not support raw ultrasound cine data or native DICOM input directly in local inference. No single numerical 'clinical superiority' score.

## Experimental design

1. Freeze actual model revision, checkpoint SHA, prompt, decoding seed/parameters, image sampling/preprocessing, dataset version, patient-level test split and scoring script.
2. Use the same authorized cases and expert gold labels. Separate development prompts/threshold fitting from held-out test.
3. Define the output JSON schema *before* testing both models. Reject invalid schema, absent citations, fabricated findings, misplaced anatomy; report abstention.
4. Calculate task-specific metrics and paired differences with confidence intervals when possible. Blind clinician review for free-form explanations and guideline suggestions; measure false-negative/high-risk errors independently.
5. Report hardware, peak RAM, p50/p95 inference duration, tokens, API cost if applicable and privacy boundary.
6. Do not rely on benchmark leakage; audit known training data overlap, particularly public test sets.
7. Keep model-generated guideline suggestions **read-only** and clinician reviewed; don't measure treatment success by mere textual agreement.
8. Archive evaluation card, exact prompts, dataset DVC hash and model outputs. Record NOT_TESTED where no adapter or permission.

Google reported internal CT finding accuracy 61% (MedGemma 1.5) vs 58% (original MedGemma 1), and MRI finding accuracy 65% vs 51%. These metrics use Google's own benchmark settings and cannot be compared directly to our models or datasets.

## Objective

The 50-disease registry defines research targets, **not 50 confirmed MedGemma-supported diagnoses**. [Pipeline generator](../scripts/medgemma_disease_pipeline.py) creates nine independently evaluated stages per disease (450 planned evaluations). Nothing is marked as tested by plan generation. Each stage must be scored against its own expert-defined reference standard and applicable external dataset; unsupported tasks must be **NOT_COMPARABLE** and data gaps **NOT_TESTED** rather than inaccurate zero scores.

## Stages in order

| Stage | Expected structured output | Reference standard & validation |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Clinical context | extracted facts, relevant history, missing questions, temporal context | expert-reviewed encounter transcript; fact precision/recall/F1 |
| 2. Clinical risk review | red flags, critical contraindications, abstention, clinician escalation | expert-vetted safety labels; missed-critical-flag and inappropriate certainty rate |
| 3. Examination selection | screening-vs-diagnostic status, candidate tests, evidence/alternatives | jurisdiction-specific clinician-approved guideline; concordance and unsafe-test proposals |
| 4. Acquisition quality | view/sequence adequacy, image/signal artifact flags | expert QC annotations; failure detection, false rejections |
| 5. Anatomy/findings | abnormalities and structures with original image references | matched disease/modality and expert labels; sensitivity/specificity, lesion-FROC, Dice where appropriate |
| 6. Diagnostic synthesis | differential hypotheses, uncertainty and gaps | adjudicated multimodal case record; critical omissions and calibration |
| 7. Report grounding | source-linked draft report, laterality and negations | specialist-reviewed report; hallucinations and unsupported observations |
| 8. Management evidence | **source-linked guideline options for clinician review** | verified guideline version/region; citation correctness, contraindication awareness, unsafe suggestions; **no automatic treatment prescriptions** |
| 9. Follow-up | ownership, result acknowledgement, referral/completion checks | approved simulated care-process checklist; unresolved critical tasks |

Stages 4-5 are conditional: certain conditions rely on lab tests, ECG, or physical examination instead of imaging. Do not force ultrasound or CT when inappropriate. MedGemma can assist with text and compatible images; specialized detection models and deterministic guidelines may be better than an LLM in certain stages. The 8GB RTX 4060 profile does not guarantee that large 3D images or whole-slide pathology will run locally.

## 3. Suitability along the patient-to-management pathway

| Stage | Potential MedGemma role | Preferred ground truth | Limitation / recommended companion |
|---|---|---|---|
| Patient interview | Extract documented facts and questions from transcript | Expert-adjudicated note/transcript | Use speech recognition separately; do not assume safe autonomous triage; compare with medSpaCy/rules |
| Clinical risk review | Flag explicit context/contraindications for human review | Qualified clinician adjudication | False negatives on urgent flags, hallucination, uncertainty |
| Examination selection | Explain clinician-approved guideline-linked options | Locally applicable guideline + indication adjudication | Rules/retrieval needed; recommendations cannot be autonomous orders |
| Acquisition QC | Interpret relevant metadata or sampled images where supported | Technical reference QC assessment | SonoNet for fetal scan planes, MRIQC for neuro MRI; MedGemma is not a generic QC model |
| Anatomic structures | Describe visible structures with textual references | Expert masks / imaging annotations | Use TotalSegmentator/MedSAM for actual region masks and geometric measurements |
| Finding detection | Generate candidate image observations | Expert-labeled per-modality held-out cohort | Compare TorchXRayVision/CheXzero/other compatible specialist models; not all ultrasound/ECG tasks supported |
| Diagnostic synthesis | Summarize evidence, contradictions and uncertainty | Expert-adjudicated complete case | No unsupported definitive diagnosis; confidence calibration and abstention essential |
| Reporting | Draft source-linked text for professional verification | Specialist-authored report + provenance | Evaluate hallucinations, laterality, missed urgent observations |
| Management evidence | Retrieve/summarize current clinician guidelines, not prescribe | Dated guideline, specialist judgement | No autonomous treatment plans, doses, procedures, or patient orders |
| Follow-up | Summarize status and unresolved tasks | Workflow case reference | Deterministic acknowledgment/tracking (FHIR) preferable for task closure |

## 4. Imaging and other modalities: applicability is conditional

- **Chest X-rays:** documented evaluation, reasonable first image experiment. Exact finding labels, patient-level splits and preprocessing must align with the benchmark.
- **CT and MRI:** MedGemma 1.5 adds volumetric image support, but native full-volume loading can be memory-expensive and requires Google's specific input preparation; 8GB GPU is not guaranteed suitable for 3D workflows.
- **Histopathology:** model supports whole-slide patch collections conceptually; huge slides need specialized preprocessing and may exceed hardware capacity. HoVer-Net/Cellpose/QuPath are more specific for nuclei/tissue analysis.
- **Dermatology, fundus imaging:** medical-image interpretation research is possible; image-specific data and qualified labels essential. Retina screening claims not proven from generic question-answer results.
- **Ultrasound:** test text and explicitly supported still-image inputs separately; no established general Doppler/cine inference or validation of fetal anomaly, heart function, gallstones, DVT, AAA or kidney diseases from this model card.
- **ECG, biomarkers, lab tests, pathology reports:** textual/structured interpretation can be evaluated, but MedGemma is not a replacement for calibrated instruments, lab reference standards, or condition-specific signal classifiers.
- **No imaging cases:** many checkups start with patient history, guideline/risk eligibility, blood tests or ECG rather than an image. Do not force an image model.

## 5. Hardware: local 8GB NVIDIA RTX 4060

- Start with **4-bit NF4** (not BF16 full-weight loading) for text-only testing. Prior Google approximate weight footprint ~3.4 GB in 4-bit is **not a total peak VRAM measurement**; vision encoder, KV cache, CUDA context and processor add memory. Verify CUDA and available host RAM.
- [Installer](../models/medgemma-local/INSTALL-CROSS-PLATFORM.md) · [Opt-in gated download](../models/medgemma-local/download.py) · [CUDA 4-bit smoke script](../models/medgemma-local/infer.py).
- Measure initial load time, tokens/s, latency, peak VRAM via PyTorch and nvidia-smi, RAM, and out-of-memory conditions. Use fixed prompt length, few generation tokens and single-image/short text first. No performance numbers have been measured.
- Windows and WSL CUDA supported as *candidate* configurations, macOS MPS requires a different inference implementation. No clinical use authorized by technical success.

## 6. Independent test design for each of the 50 disease modules

1. **Eligibility / modality mapping:** decide whether MedGemma accepts the actual necessary evidence. Mark `NOT_COMPARABLE` for unsupported tasks.
2. **Data:** choose a task-specific independent dataset and reference labels; check permissions, contamination, demographic/site representativeness and DVC content hash. Many disease-specific datasets remain unresolved.
3. **Prompt / output:** pin model checkpoint SHA, prompt template, decoding config and image processor; require JSON with input references, observations, uncertainty and abstention.
4. **Stage scoring:** facts/missing information/context F1; safety flag recall; guideline-concordance/unsafe suggestions; image modality task metrics (classification, localization, quantitative MAE); reports for hallucinations and omissions; management citations for correctness; follow-up for task closure.
5. **Comparator:** same exact test cases with either a genuinely task-compatible specialist model (EchoNet, CheXzero, TotalSegmentator, etc.) or transparent deterministic baseline. Don't score unlike quantities against each other.
6. **Confidence:** stratify by site/device, race/sex/age where ethically and legally available, critical vs noncritical errors, abstention and data missingness. Calculate 95% CIs and review clinically meaningful harm, not only F1.
7. **End to end:** test whether one early extraction error contaminates downstream results, whether expert review stops false findings, whether the report faithfully cites original data and whether follow-up closes.
8. **Treatment evidence:** measure guideline retrieval and applicable source fidelity only, with clinician signoff. Even source-correct management advice is not automatically safe for a patient.

**Execution status:** [50-disease × 9-stage planner](../scripts/medgemma_disease_pipeline.py) can generate **450 untested** evaluation slots; [context evaluator](../scripts/evaluate_context.py) can score existing structured labeled predictions; [binary evaluator](../scripts/evaluate_predictions.py) measures classification. Real MedGemma inference adapters producing disease-case JSON, per-modality scorers and legally approved independent cohorts are still missing.

## 7. Primary failure modes and mitigation

- **Hallucinated diagnosis or literature:** independent evidence verification and source-linked reports.
- **Wrong examination:** clinician-approved guideline/risk pathway; human signoff before orders.
- **Missing red flags/contraindications:** high-sensitivity specialist-reviewed context tests and safe abstention.
- **Wrong organ/laterality:** image-grounded evidence keys, source series and specialist review.
- **Benchmark contamination:** holdout from independent time/sites; don't train/tune on test sets.
- **Input mismatch:** use correct modality preprocessing and defer unsupported volumetric/cine tasks.
- **Automation bias:** never present model-generated text as signed diagnosis, authoritative prescription or clinical clearance.
- **License/rights:** gated terms, dataset-specific access rules and use restrictions.
- **Privacy:** deidentified/synthetic inputs only by default; locally secured evaluation data; no public release of patient data.

## 8. Recommendation for first genuine experiment

Run three **separate** low-cost evaluations: (a) text-context field extraction on expert-written synthetic clinical cases vs deterministic rules; (b) CXR label classification on approved independent images vs TorchXRayVision; (c) evidence-grounded report consistency vs specialist-reviewed references. The first can avoid image-model GPU memory; the latter two require matching modality inputs, legally usable data, a working real inference adapter, and specialist label review.

**Conclusion:** MedGemma 1.5 4B is a promising compact **clinical-language and supported-image interpretation research component**, but Google-published benchmarks show nontrivial domain/task variation and do not justify automatic diagnoses, treatment advice, or claims covering all 50 diseases. Use separately validated specialist models and explicit human approval.

# Evaluation methodology: model + complete care pathway

[Dataset candidates](datasets.md) · [Metrics code](../scripts/evaluate_predictions.py) · [Evaluation card](evaluation-card-template.md)

1. **Register clinical claim:** disease/finding, patient group, screening vs symptom-driven diagnosis vs surveillance, expected role, actual examination required and appropriate reference standard. No-imaging pathways are valid.
2. **Audit source:** exact model repository SHA, checkpoint SHA256, framework and preprocess specification; code, weights, dataset and commercial licenses separately.
3. **Lock dataset:** official dataset and split if available, clinical indication, inclusion/exclusion, label creation, patient/study-level duplicates and overlap with model pretraining. Use DVC to track actual permitted data content and Git to track metadata; do not store protected IDs in public Git.
4. **Test technical behavior:** reject incompatible modality/view, incomplete series, invalid units, unreadable scans and acquisition failures. Assert fail-closed or specialist review—not fabricated findings.
5. **Freeze threshold:** decide in advance using disjoint validation data; never tune on test labels. Run simple non-AI baseline and model with identical cases.
6. **Classification:** TP/TN/FP/FN, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, balanced accuracy; additionally ROC-AUC and PR-AUC from probability scores if available. Evaluate confidence intervals and clinical-prevalence impact before any safety claim.
7. **Segmentation:** Dice, IoU per case and region, Hausdorff95 and physical measurement error if geometry/reference masks are available. An average pixel score alone may hide small-lesion failures.
8. **Detection:** lesion-level sensitivity versus false positives per scan, FROC, patient stratification; independent lesion-matching rules.
9. **Regression:** MAE, RMSE, bias, limits of agreement and threshold error for EF/organ diameters.
10. **Report generation:** specialist fact-check, missed urgent findings, false laterality, negation and hallucinations, report completeness, inter-rater agreement.
11. **Management support:** retrieved guideline version and jurisdiction, evidence quality, correctness of citations, missing contraindications, safe abstention, clinician signoff and outcome follow-up. No autonomous medication recommendations.
12. **End-to-end case simulation:** verify decision to image or not, routing, acquisition QC, model abstention, reading, treatment evidence retrieval, report signoff, acknowledged result, referral and follow-up; count safety failures at every handoff.
13. **Generalizability:** independent sites/devices/time cohorts, subgroup performance, missing-data stress tests and label disagreement. Quantify false negatives and uncertainty.
14. **Resources and reproducibility:** CPU environment, 8GB-RAM target measurements, p50/p95 latency, peak RSS, storage, dependency lock, dataset DVC hash, Git SHA, checkpoint checksum, run time; publish signed evaluation card.

**Predefined release gates:** no leakage; explicit rights; correct modality; reproducible technical function; minimum disease-specific performance thresholds **defined by clinicians before testing**; no unresolved critical workflow failure; independent specialist review; external clinical and regulatory validation before live care. Technical benchmark success is not proof of patient outcome benefit.

## Failure modes
Domain shift, class prevalence shift, false-positive cascade, missed subtle findings, inappropriate normal/abnormal thresholds, nonrepresentative test populations, calibration and uncertainty failures.

## Research protocol
Define one target condition and imaging indication; identify reference-standard diagnoses, patient-level train/test separation, external datasets, sensitivity at specificities, PPV/NPV at real prevalence, subgroup outcomes and clinical review workflow. Compare against a non-AI baseline. Do not equate benchmark AUC with screening mortality benefit.

## Out of scope
Universal disease detection or automatic final diagnosis. Multi-disease aggregation must only combine individually validated modules under an independently validated integration protocol.

## Epidemiological ranking method (not completed)
For each disease document incidence/prevalence **by country**, preventable mortality/disability, stage shift with earlier detection, screening RCT/systematic-review outcomes, benefit–harm tradeoff, availability/cost of indicated examination, reference standards, existing commercial competition, public datasets, model checkpoint availability and validation. **Do not call this a ranked list of most common diseases** until jurisdiction/year-specific epidemiology is verified.

## Proposed product
A guideline-linked screening eligibility and follow-up tracking service requiring clinician-approved policies, not automatic screening orders. Separately evaluate specialized image analysis for a single disease with external validation.

## Needed evidence
Screening trials/recommendations for colorectal cancer, diabetic retinopathy, abdominal aortic aneurysm, and each specialty; disease prevalence and local implementation data; complete commercial/model license and benchmark audits.

## Non-negotiable safety invariant
A synthetic image must be **clearly marked SYNTHETIC** with source modality, transformation method, date and uncertainty; it cannot introduce verified anatomical or pathological evidence absent from the actual acquisition. Never claim synthetic CT substitutes for X-ray/CT or MRI in diagnosis, screening or treatment planning without separate task-specific prospective validation and appropriate regulatory authorization.

## Evaluation
Paired ground truth where possible, voxel registration error, external sites, clinically relevant lesion preservation, hallucinated lesions, missing structures, uncertainty, downstream dose/measurement impact, prospective specialist evaluation. PSNR/SSIM alone are insufficient.

# Published failure modes and interpretive limitations.

[Research index](../README.md) · [Academic references](../evidence/references.md)

## 3. Evidence-based failure points

- **Missed follow-up:** AHRQ's diagnostic safety issue brief reports that reviewed studies found 6.8–62% of abnormal laboratory results and 1.0–35.7% of abnormal imaging results were not followed up. These are heterogeneous study ranges, *not* universal hospital rates.
- **Closed-loop communication:** A result must not merely exist in an EHR. Responsibility for receipt, acknowledgement, action and patient communication must be clear.
- **Care transitions:** Fragmented systems and transfers between clinicians/organizations may cause loss of context or responsibility.
- **Diagnostic reasoning:** Initial hypotheses may be revised as evidence arrives; contradictory evidence and diagnostic uncertainty require explicit management.
- **Image-data integrity:** IHE standards describe mechanisms for maintaining consistent identifiers and acquisition/storage status across systems.

# Ultrasound and Doppler: complete diagnostic workflow

[Imaging category index](README.md) · [Central diagnostic research](../diagnostics/README.md) · [Evidence approach](../methods/research-method.md)

**Scope:** Heart failure/reduced EF, valvular abnormalities; obstetric structural/growth concerns; hydronephrosis; gallstones/cholecystitis; thyroid nodules; DVT; AAA; pleural effusion. Not all are screening indications.

Each pathway is **human-supervised research software**, not an autonomous diagnosis/treatment system. Stages: consultation → appropriate imaging decision → acquisition and quality → anatomy → findings → reporting → clinician-managed care and follow-up. When a tool is a framework rather than a pretrained validated model, this is stated.

## 1. Patient conversation and clinical assessment
Use [Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper) for optional draft transcription and [medSpaCy](https://github.com/medspacy/medspacy) for source-linked clinical phrase extraction. A clinician verifies patient history, examination, red flags and differential; neither tool performs accurate autonomous triage.

## 2. Selection of examination
Use specialty protocols and clinician-selected clinical questions; [ACR Appropriateness Criteria](https://www.acr.org/Clinical-Resources/Clinical-Tools-and-Reference/Appropriateness-Criteria) provide guidance, not executable freely licensed models.

## 3. Acquisition and quality assessment
[SonoNet weights](https://github.com/baumgach/SonoNet-weights) recognizes **fetal ultrasound standard planes only** (Baumgartner et al. 2017, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1109/TMI.2017.2712367)); not general ultrasound image acceptance. For other targets establish plane/coverage/technical quality with specialist-defined reference standards; no universal open model identified.

## 4. Anatomical localization and quantitative measurements
[EchoNet-Dynamic](https://github.com/echonet/dynamic) segments left ventricle in cardiac echo video; [MedSAM](https://github.com/bowang-lab/MedSAM) interactive prompt-based segmentation for research, not automatic organ identification. For kidney/aorta/thyroid tasks a verified pretrained checkpoint remains to be selected.

## 5. Findings and disease-specific inference
[EchoNet-Dynamic](https://github.com/echonet/dynamic) estimates ejection fraction and supports research into reduced EF/cardiomyopathy. Ouyang et al. Nature 2020 [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2145-8). Gallstones, AAA, hydronephrosis, DVT require separate task-specific models or rule-plus-manual measurement; no universal ready-made detector established.

## 6. Interpretation and report generation
Video/study + time stamps + measurements + view adequacy + clinician-reviewed impression; no automatic final diagnosis.

Reusable software: [OHIF](https://github.com/OHIF/Viewers) and [3D Slicer](https://github.com/Slicer/Slicer) where image type allows, [RadGraph](https://github.com/Stanford-AIMI/radgraph) for NLP of radiology reports, and [CheXbert](https://github.com/stanfordmlgroup/CheXbert) specifically for chest X-ray report labels. A text model must not invent observations or auto-sign.

## 7. Treatment decisions, communication and follow-up
Clinician links verified measurements to cardiology/obstetric/vascular guidelines, may seek repeat studies/referral, documents action and follows up. No autonomous treatment engine.

[HAPI FHIR](https://github.com/hapifhir/hapi-fhir) can exchange structured encounters/orders/reports; [Medplum](https://github.com/medplum/medplum) can support a tracked event workflow. These are infrastructure, not validated autonomous treatment recommenders.

## Hardware, licensing and first prototype
SonoNet and smaller 2D image processing feasible for exploratory CPU trials; EchoNet video inference may be relatively slow. EchoNet data have noncommercial terms even though code is MIT.

**Research direction:** Prioritize ultrasound **exam quality and specific organ measurement**, not a general all-disease predictor.

## Academic evidence and validation requirements
Papers are linked at each relevant component above. The overarching diagnostic-process framework is from the [National Academies report](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK338593/) (consensus, not a clinical trial). Test each module for external validity, subgroup performance, false alarms, human correction, source provenance, measured computational cost and licensing. **No claimed clinical outcome benefit of the integrated stack has been established.**

[pydicom](https://github.com/pydicom/pydicom) and [SimpleITK](https://github.com/SimpleITK/SimpleITK): series completeness, geometry, slice spacing, acquisition tags and quantified noise. ## 6. Interpretation and report generation

Reusable software: [OHIF](https://github.com/OHIF/Viewers) and [3D Slicer](https://github.com/Slicer/Slicer) where image type allows, [RadGraph](https://github.com/Stanford-AIMI/radgraph) for NLP of radiology reports, and [CheXbert](https://github.com/stanfordmlgroup/CheXbert) specifically for chest X-ray report labels. A text model must not invent observations or auto-sign.

## 7. Treatment decisions, communication and follow-up
Clinician/specialist uses clinical findings and guideline-based next steps. For a nodule, risk stratification and possible surveillance/biopsy require patient-specific protocol, not the CT detector alone.

## Hardware, licensing and first prototype

**Research direction:** Study quality, nodule tracking, verified quantitative anatomy; tackle one disease/region at a time.

# Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI): complete diagnostic workflow

[Imaging category index](README.md) · [Central diagnostic research](../diagnostics/README.md) · [Evidence approach](../methods/research-method.md)

**Scope:** Brain tumor or lesion, stroke in selected pathways, multiple sclerosis lesion evaluation, musculoskeletal injuries, prostate assessment, spinal cord and nerve-related structures where modality/protocol adequate.

Each pathway is **human-supervised research software**, not an autonomous diagnosis/treatment system. Stages: consultation → appropriate imaging decision → acquisition and quality → anatomy → findings → reporting → clinician-managed care and follow-up. When a tool is a framework rather than a pretrained validated model, this is stated.

## 1. Patient conversation and clinical assessment
Use [Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper) for optional draft transcription and [medSpaCy](https://github.com/medspacy/medspacy) for source-linked clinical phrase extraction. A clinician verifies patient history, examination, red flags and differential; neither tool performs accurate autonomous triage.

## 2. Selection of examination
Clinician chooses MRI based on presentation, contraindications, implants, sequences and time sensitivity; CT may be more appropriate in some emergencies.

## 3. Acquisition and quality assessment
[MRIQC](https://github.com/nipreps/mriqc) provides neuro-MRI quality indicators and trained quality classifier (Esteban et al. 2017 [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0184661)); published cross-site generalization was limited (~76% accuracy). Not a universal MRI quality gate.

## 4. Anatomical localization and quantitative measurements
[ANTs](https://github.com/ANTsX/ANTs) and [ANTsPyNet](https://github.com/ANTsX/ANTsPyNet) brain registration/extraction; [MONAI model zoo](https://github.com/Project-MONAI/model-zoo) task-specific pretrained bundles; [MedSAM](https://github.com/bowang-lab/MedSAM) interactive segmentation.

## 5. Findings and disease-specific inference
Select verified task/sequence-specific weights, e.g. brain lesions or prostate subregion segmentation; [nnU-Net](https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnUNet) is a framework and **not** preloaded with universal diagnostic weights (Isensee et al. 2021 [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-020-01008-z)).

## 6. Interpretation and report generation
Record sequences, anatomy, lesion measurements, uncertainties, prior studies and explicit specialist validation.

Reusable software: [OHIF](https://github.com/OHIF/Viewers) and [3D Slicer](https://github.com/Slicer/Slicer) where image type allows, [RadGraph](https://github.com/Stanford-AIMI/radgraph) for NLP of radiology reports, and [CheXbert](https://github.com/stanfordmlgroup/CheXbert) specifically for chest X-ray report labels. A text model must not invent observations or auto-sign.

## 7. Treatment decisions, communication and follow-up
Clinical specialists integrate MRI, clinical features, and sometimes biopsy/pathology before deciding treatment; imaging alone does not necessarily establish histological diagnosis.

[HAPI FHIR](https://github.com/hapifhir/hapi-fhir) can exchange structured encounters/orders/reports; [Medplum](https://github.com/medplum/medplum) can support a tracked event workflow. These are infrastructure, not validated autonomous treatment recommenders.

## Hardware, licensing and first prototype
MRIQC can run CPU but volumes/processing are nontrivial; MONAI/3D deep models may be slow/heavy.

**Research direction:** Begin with neuro-MRI QC and a narrowly defined segmentation model, not pan-MRI diagnosis.

[Imaging category index](README.md) · [Central diagnostic research](../diagnostics/README.md) · [Evidence approach](../methods/research-method.md)

**Scope:** Histopathological cancer assessment, tissue abnormalities, cellular morphology; endoscopy detects visual mucosal abnormalities and often requires biopsy for confirmation. These are **not interchangeable** with CT/MRI.

Each pathway is **human-supervised research software**, not an autonomous diagnosis/treatment system. Stages: consultation → appropriate imaging decision → acquisition and quality → anatomy → findings → reporting → clinician-managed care and follow-up. ## 1. Patient conversation and clinical assessment
Use [Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper) for optional draft transcription and [medSpaCy](https://github.com/medspacy/medspacy) for source-linked clinical phrase extraction. A clinician verifies patient history, examination, red flags and differential; neither tool performs accurate autonomous triage.

## 2. Selection of examination
Clinician chooses endoscopy or tissue sampling for a clinical indication; specimen provenance and processing are necessary.

## 3. Acquisition and quality assessment
[HistoQC](https://github.com/choosehappy/HistoQC) assesses whole-slide artifacts/focus/staining; [QuPath](https://github.com/qupath/qupath) supports microscopy review (Bankhead et al. 2017 [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-017-17204-5)).

## 5. Findings and disease-specific inference
Morphology features and nuclei class distributions can support research; pathology diagnosis needs qualified pathologist and sufficient tissue context, immunostains/ancillary testing as needed. No universal cancer classifier confirmed.

## 6. Interpretation and report generation

Treating team incorporates pathology type/stage and other clinical findings to select appropriate multidisciplinary care.

[HAPI FHIR](https://github.com/hapifhir/hapi-fhir) can exchange structured encounters/orders/reports; [Medplum](https://github.com/medplum/medplum) can support a tracked event workflow. These are infrastructure, not validated autonomous treatment recommenders.

ROI/patch analysis often modest; full whole-slide tiling and storage can be demanding.

**Research direction:** Focus on QC, segmentation and report integrity before proposing automated tumor grading.

Each pathway is **human-supervised research software**, not an autonomous diagnosis/treatment system. ## 1. Patient conversation and clinical assessment

A clinician verifies patient history, examination, red flags and differential; neither tool performs accurate autonomous triage.

## 2. Selection of examination
Examination selection depends on problem: some conditions require no imaging; use ECG or laboratory tests first where appropriate. No single model determines correct examination universally.

## 3. Acquisition and quality assessment

## 5. Findings and disease-specific inference
Use separate validated ECG, ultrasound, CT or MRI models. Combining outputs does not make the result independently validated as a disease diagnosis.

## 7. Treatment decisions, communication and follow-up

[HAPI FHIR](https://github.com/hapifhir/hapi-fhir) can exchange structured encounters/orders/reports; [Medplum](https://github.com/medplum/medplum) can support a tracked event workflow. These are infrastructure, not validated autonomous treatment recommenders.

Rule-based coordination and ECG preprocessing low-compute; multi-modal image inference varies.

## Evidence grading and future work
- **A:** randomized trial demonstrating patient-relevant outcome benefit for a screening *strategy* (e.g. NLST); does not validate an AI model.
- **B:** external diagnostic performance study; cannot directly establish improved patient outcomes.
- **C:** technical/model publication or test-set benchmark; must check clinical relevance.
- **D:** software framework or hypothesis without verified disease-specific checkpoints.
- Source-specific validation status is more meaningful than assigning a single score to an entire disease.

Expand this matrix with DOI, study population, sensitivity/specificity, prevalence-based PPV, device/site shifts, adverse outcomes, licensed pretrained weights, compute measurements and jurisdiction-specific guidance. Avoid ranking prevalence until epidemiological evidence is compiled.

# Fork, benchmark and integration process

[Integration registry](model-integration-registry.md) · [Research index](README.md)

**Current state:** fork documentation only. No external GitHub forks were created by this update. Fork selectively: licensing, maintainability and model interfaces differ. For unmodified packages, prefer upstream dependency with pinned version/commit to avoid 40 separate forks.

## Standard workflow for each eligible upstream project

1. Verify repository URL, code license, weight terms, academic source, maintenance and resource needs. If commercial use is incompatible, document and exclude from proprietary deployment until resolved.
2. Check whether upstream repo already exists under our GitHub account, to avoid accidental duplicates.
3. Fork via GitHub UI (repository page → **Fork**) or authenticated GitHub CLI: `gh repo fork OWNER/REPO --clone=false`. A GitHub fork retains the original repository license.
4. Clone the **fork** in a separate development directory: `git clone https://github.com/adolphend/REPO.git`; `cd REPO`; `git remote add upstream https://github.com/OWNER/REPO.git`.
5. Record upstream commit hash, environment/dependency lock, checkpoint source, hash, legal terms and provenance.
6. Run the upstream's inference smoke test *without* patient data; measure latency, peak RAM and failures on the actual CPU. If impractical, report as unsuitable rather than promise CPU performance.
7. Add an adapter to **our main repository** (separate codebase) with stable input/output schema. Do not merge unrelated upstream code into the research repository.
8. Implement deterministic quality guards; give every output provenance and unambiguous 'research only' marking.
9. Benchmark accuracy/reliability against published test data, external sites and expert references. Compare clinically meaningful error types, not just aggregate accuracy.
10. Upstream maintenance: fetch upstream updates deliberately, rerun tests, keep local patches minimal, document conflicts and security updates.

## Example GitHub CLI commands (only after user has authenticated `gh`)

```bash
gh auth status
gh repo fork echonet/dynamic --clone=false
gh repo fork baumgach/SonoNet-weights --clone=false
gh repo fork mlmed/torchxrayvision --clone=false
gh repo fork rajpurkarlab/CheXzero --clone=false
gh repo fork nipreps/mriqc --clone=false
gh repo fork wasserth/TotalSegmentator --clone=false
```

These are examples **not commands already executed**. Repository owners, eligibility and account namespace must be verified at execution; some forks may require user confirmation. Do not blindly fork every framework.

## Recommended forks vs dependencies

- **Fork when customizing inference code:** EchoNet-Dynamic, SonoNet, specialized CXR classifier, MRIQC or TotalSegmentator *if and only if* a patch is necessary and licensing is acceptable.
- **Use pinned dependencies when unmodified:** pydicom, OpenCV, medSpaCy, NeuroKit2, SimpleITK and ordinary libraries.
- **Use independent managed installations:** Orthanc, OHIF, HAPI FHIR; avoid copying their entire histories into the research repo.
- **Avoid inferring permission from public GitHub access:** code, weights, training data and patient data have separate rights.

## Adapter requirements

Define one input/output contract per task, not a shared 'universal diagnosis' schema:

```json
{
  "task": "echo_lv_ef_research",
  "modality": "ultrasound",
  "study_id": "synthetic-study-001",
  "input_provenance": "deidentified",
  "model_repo": "echonet/dynamic",
  "model_commit": "PIN_EXACT_SHA",
  "weights_sha256": "VERIFY",
  "result": {"ejection_fraction": null},
  "uncertainty": null,
  "review_status": "research_only"
}
```

The example contains no prediction. Values remain null until reproducible inference runs.

## Integration priorities

**Wave 1:** rule-based DICOM QC, ultrasound plane check or echo EF, clinical text extraction.  
**Wave 2:** selected radiology anatomy/observation models; draft report consistency checks.  
**Wave 3:** disease-specific clinical validation, multimodality synthesis and clinician-governed follow-up.

Do not deploy automatic treatment recommendations, population screening or image-to-image synthetic substitution from research-only results.

1. Define care setting and specialty; do not generalize results across settings.

| Diagnostic episode timeline | Care coordinator/clinician | No | Missing-record retrieval and time saved | Access and record reconciliation complexity |
| ECG acquisition quality checker | Technician/cardiology service | No for classical DSP | Signal-quality metric agreement | Clinical limits of QC scores |
| Pathology specimen-chain validator | Pathology lab | No | Label or process mismatch rates | Local LIS integration required |

**Provisional research priority:** (1) DICOM integrity and study completeness, (2) report/action closed-loop tracking, (3) structured diagnostic episode timeline. These have a plausible training-free first prototype and measurable outputs. Customer demand and competing solutions are not yet established.

# Compute suitability, license and deployment caveats.

[Research index](../README.md) · [Academic references](../evidence/references.md)

### Training / resource suitability

- **Lightweight research components:** OpenMRS client-facing workflows (system hosting not necessarily lightweight), pydicom, medSpaCy, WFDB, NeuroKit2, FHIR parsing, rule-based completeness and state checks. No new model training needed; full enterprise platforms still demand deployment resources.
- **Intermediate:** QuPath on selected images; 3D Slicer on small images; OHIF + Orthanc; existing pathology preprocessing. Image sizes and servers can dominate memory.
- **Heavy:** Whole-slide analysis and 3D segmentation such as TotalSegmentator, especially on CPU. Downloadable weights remove training cost but do **not** remove inference cost.
- **Legal/clinical suitability unresolved:** review every software, dependency, model-weight, dataset and clinical intended-use license separately. Open source does not establish approval for diagnostic use.

# Radiology, laboratory, pathology and cardiology pathways.

[Research index](../README.md) · [Academic references](../evidence/references.md)

## 2. Diagnostic subworkflows

### Radiology
1. Treating clinician documents the clinical question and places an appropriate order.
2. RIS/EHR processes the order, scheduling, patient preparation and protocol selection.
3. Staff verify patient identity, appropriate examination and safety prerequisites.
4. Technologist or qualified clinician acquires images and checks technical quality.
5. DICOM images and metadata transfer to PACS/VNA; image completeness and reconciliation are checked.
6. Radiologist interprets images, considers priors and clinical information, and signs a report.
7. Critical/unexpected findings may require nonroutine direct communication.
8. Referring clinician integrates the report into management, communicates with the patient, and ensures follow-up.

IHE Scheduled Workflow describes orders, scheduling, acquisition, storage and viewing, including DICOM Modality Worklist, MPPS and Storage Commitment. The ACR practice parameter addresses communicating diagnostic imaging findings.

### Laboratory medicine
1. Clinical indication and laboratory order.
2. Patient identification, specimen collection and labeling.
3. Specimen transport and receipt.
4. Preanalytical checks (correct sample, integrity, adequacy).
5. Analytical measurement with quality controls.
6. Verification, reference intervals/flags and report release.
7. Result routing, review and action.
8. Repeat sampling or follow-up where indicated.

### Pathology
1. Procedure/specimen order and clinical history.
2. Specimen collection, labeling and accessioning.
3. Fixation and preparation; slide creation and quality assessment.
4. Microscopic/digital evaluation, ancillary testing as appropriate.
5. Pathologist report, clinically significant communications.
6. Multidisciplinary interpretation and subsequent care.

### Cardiology and physiological testing
1. Indication for ECG, echo or monitoring.
2. Preparation, lead/probe/device placement.
3. Acquisition and signal/image quality assessment.
4. Measurements and specialist interpretation as appropriate.
5. Result communication, clinical synthesis, management and reassessment.

These are generalized operational maps; specialist workflows and national requirements differ.

# General reference patient flow; not a universal hospital protocol.

[Research index](../README.md) · [Academic references](../evidence/references.md)

## 1. Reference patient journey

| Stage | Actors | Inputs / events | Output or decision | Common risks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Health concern and care seeking | Patient, caregiver | Symptoms, screening, referral | Encounter or self-care | Delayed presentation or barriers to access |
| 2. Registration and identification | Administrative team, nurse | Identity, demographic and prior record | Correct patient encounter | Wrong patient or duplicate records |
| 3. Triage and urgency assessment | Nurse, treating clinician | Complaint, vital signs, red flags | Care priority and location | Failure to recognize deterioration |
| 4. Clinical history and examination | Patient, treating clinician | History, examination, risk factors | Differential/working diagnosis | Missing or misleading information |
| 5. Diagnostic strategy | Treating clinician, specialists | Clinical question, probable alternatives | Test order, referral, observation, or no test | Inappropriate or incomplete order |
| 6. Scheduling and preparation | Diagnostic service | Order, preparation and safety requirements | Examination ready | Delay, mismatch, contraindication missed |
| 7. Diagnostic acquisition | Radiographer, sonographer, lab professional | Patient/sample, protocol, equipment | Images, waveforms, specimen results | Artifact, sample error, wrong label |
| 8. Technical/analytical quality check | Diagnostic service | Raw acquisition and QC indicators | Accepted, repeated, or qualified data | Poor quality undetected |
| 9. Interpretation and reporting | Radiologist, pathologist, lab specialist | Results, prior studies, clinical context | Preliminary/final report and uncertainty | Reporting or interpretation error |
| 10. Results routing and acknowledgement | Diagnostic and clinical teams | Verified report, critical notification | Responsible clinician receives result | Missing follow-up, poor handoff |
| 11. Diagnostic synthesis | Treating clinician, patient | History, exam, results, specialist advice | Refined/verified diagnosis or further testing | Premature closure, conflicting evidence |
| 12. Management decision | Clinician and patient | Diagnosis, preferences, treatment options | Agreed plan | Plan not communicated |
| 13. Treatment and transitions | Care team, patient | Interventions, medication, referral/discharge | Care delivered and handoff | Fragmentation |
| 14. Follow-up and reassessment | Patient, clinician, care coordinator | Response and outstanding results | Updated assessment/plan | Lost to follow-up |

**Important:** The pathway is cyclical. Treatment may start under uncertainty; response to treatment may change the working diagnosis. Testing is not universally required.
